correctness.rationale: For all n≥3, exact outside-vertex neighbor counts prove that the only minimal forts are each pure three-set from either part and each matching-aligned four-set indexed by two positions. The fort-obstruction equivalence gives all zero-forcing sets and the minimal/maximal-failed classifications. Labeled counting produces the square-minus-diagonal polynomial. An explicit packing achieves floor(2n/3), and the uniform one-third feasible fractional cover together with the summed pure-triple constraints proves Z*=2n/3. The proof treats n=3 without exceptional assumptions. All 87,360 vertex subsets of n=3..8 were directly checked, and packings for n=3..7 were independently optimized; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The matching-deleted biclique is a natural regular bipartite family whose complete fort-obstruction hypergraph was not supplied by the inspected family literature. Its closed polynomial counts all zero-forcing sets, not only minima. The parameter shift from K_{n,n} is asymmetrical: the ordinary number drops by two, the fractional number drops by n/3, and their ratio tends to three. The new exact packing and well-forced classification are mathematically interpretable consequences of one structural theorem rather than routine unrelated special cases.
